content.comment_body: Hello, is there any way to send an HTTP request from [product_name]? If that's not possible, I considered using it together with a Teltonika VPN router. The idea is to have [product_name] communicate with Teltonika via Modbus, and then send the HTTP POST alarm to the server through the Teltonika modem. I don't need to transfer specific data from [product_name], just trigger a simple HTTP request to a specified server address to let it know to read data from the unit. Thanks.

Hello, from what I understand, you want to connect to a server when an error occurs. Sending a notification only during errors (not continuously) is only possible using a specific communication module via SMS. Other options, like Modbus and [product_name], require a continuous connection between devices. For Modbus, if you set [product_name] as the client, you can adjust the communication cycle, but it will always stay connected with the other Modbus device. Hope this helps.

Hello, thank you. We have a VPN tunnel set up between the server and the unit with [product_name], so the connection is in place. I'm still looking for a way to trigger an HTTP POST to the server address whenever an alarm signal occurs. [user_name].

analysis.insight_summary: The user is investigating if [product_name] can send an HTTP request to a server when triggered by an alarm, aiming for a straightforward alarm notification solution. Replies clarify that this function isn't available directly in [product_name]; only SMS via a dedicated module or continuous Modbus/[product_name] connections are supported. Current technical limitations restrict the implementation of one-way HTTP notifications using [product_name].
analysis.user_expectations: User expects [product_name] to natively send HTTP requests or POSTs in response to alarms, rather than relying on persistent communication or repeated data polling.
